Subject: Encryption / KMS options — follow-up and next steps

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the detailed run-through of GreenLeaf's requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Recap (from today's discovery):
- Data types: app-generated telemetry + user-submitted forms that include PII (names, DOBs, partial SSNs).
- Retention: primary ask is 7-year retention for certain records; shorter windows for non-PII.
- Logging: need audit logs for admin actions and key access; logs should be able to be forwarded to GLeaf SIEM and support redaction.
- Residency: primary concern is US (multi-region offices but legal data residency is US).
- Encryption: require in-transit + at-rest encryption; evaluating customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM options.

Questions / clarifications we need from you to scope next steps:
1) Do you require keys to be stored in your cloud account (BYOK) or would a customer-managed-key model where Redwood holds a wrapped key be acceptable?
2) Do you need FIPS 140-2/3 HSM-backed key material (e.g., CloudHSM / Key Vault HSM)?
3) Are there any specific key rotation / dual-control policies we should model (e.g., rotation cadence, separation of duties)?
4) Required retention windows per data class (if you can provide a short table that would help).

Next steps I propose:
- Attached: short KMS options brief and our latest SOC 2 report for your security/compliance team to review (redwood-kms-options.pdf, SOC2-report-2025.pdf).
- Technical deep-dive with David to walk through KMS integration patterns and key residency options (30-45m).
- I can follow up with a proposed SOW/PoC outline once we confirm KMS model and retention SLAs.

Proposed times for the technical deep-dive:
- Mon 6/14 10:00-10:45 PT
- Tue 6/15 11:00-11:45 PT

If those don't work share availability and we'll adjust.

Thanks 
Marissa

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few quick answers and follow-ups from our side: 

1) Key residency: preference is keys controlled in our cloud account (BYOK) if possible — legal wants to ensure separation of control. We may consider Redwood-managed keys only if there is a strong compensating control and an auditable chain.
2) HSM: yes, preference for HSM-backed key material (FIPS 140-2 or 140-3).
3) Rotation: standard cadence is annual rotation, but we may need emergency rotation procedures (and documentation of the process).
4) Retention: I'll send a short table of required retention windows for different data classes by EOD.

A couple of clarifying questions for David/Rishi: 
- If we do BYOK with our AWS KMS account, can Redwood perform envelope encryption while keeping the customer master key (CMK) in our account?
- Are you able to provide key access logs (KMS: CloudTrail events) as part of the audit package?

We'd like the technical deep-dive next week. Tue 6/15 11:00 PT works for our team. Can you send a calendar invite + Zoom link?

Also please include any notes on how you handle PII in logs (redaction or exclusion options).

Thanks,
Alex

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Encryption / KMS options — follow-up and next steps

Alex — thanks for the quick responses. I wanted to provide more technical detail ahead of the Tue deep-dive so we can use the session for configuration decisions rather than basic architecture. Key points below: 

Transport encryption:
- All traffic to Redwood's hosted API is TLS 1.3 (we maintain TLS 1.2+ compatibility where needed). For Dedicated and Private deployments we support mTLS for client authentication.

At-rest encryption:
- We encrypt data at rest using AES-256-GCM for primary data stores and object storage.

KMS / BYOK options we support:
1) Customer-Managed Keys (recommended for your scenario):
   - Customer holds the CMK in their cloud account (e.g., AWS KMS). Redwood performs envelope encryption where your CMK is used to wrap/unwrap a data encryption key (DEK) that we manage per-tenant.
   - We support using AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and GCP KMS. For HSM-backed keys, we integrate with CloudHSM/Key Vault HSM-backed keys.
   - Key access is logged via CloudTrail / Key Vault diagnostics which can be forwarded to your SIEM.
2) Redwood-Managed Customer-Exclusive Keys:
   - For customers who want a managed path without provisioning their own KMS account we offer dedicated keys in our KMS with strict access controls and audit logs. This is still customer-isolated but Redwood holds the root CMK.
3) On-Prem / Private Deployments:
   - Full customer control: keys and key stores live inside your VPC/on-prem HSM. Redwood's private control plane can be configured to use local HSMs (we support standard PKCS#11 interfaces).

Key lifecycle and controls:
- Rotation: We support automatic scheduled rotation of DEKs and can coordinate CMK rotation workflows; emergency rotation procedures can be executed through a documented runbook and we provide playbooks for cutover.
- Separation of duties: access to CMKs requires role-based controls and can be constrained by IAM policies and conditional access.
- Exportability: CMKs in cloud HSMs follow provider constraints; we support bringing key material into supported HSMs where allowed by provider.

Logging and auditability:
- KMS events: we surface KMS operations (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey) into a structured audit feed.
- Access logs: admin/API access logs can be forwarded to your SIEM (syslog/HTTPS).
- PII in logs: by default we avoid logging full user-submitted content. Sensitive fields can be redacted at ingest (configurable). We can provide a log redaction policy and a sample redaction config in the deep-dive.

Data residency:
- For hosted deployments we support region pinning for data-at-rest and compute (we serve from US East/West, EU, and APAC regions). For strict legal requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments to guarantee physical control.

Attachments: I'll post a short technical appendix in the calendar invite with sample CloudTrail filters and an example KMS integration diagram.

See you Tue 6/15 11:00 PT — I'll bring a brief runbook and configuration checklist.

- David
